design: six frozen case questions and analyst-authored rubrics, not independently blinded; not actual experimental observations

cases.question: For the supplied portfolio, explain whether the $6m cash balance establishes adequate liquidity under a severe spread-and-rates stress. What must be checked before making a funding judgment?
required_questions: Contractual margin and collateral needs (CSA/netting, timing)
Unencumbered cash, drawable facilities and other available liquidity
Stress liquidation costs and executable market depth
unjustified_conclusions: Cash is sufficient or insufficient without obligations and terms

cases.question: The daily rates book gains while the overall portfolio loses. Has the duration hedge succeeded, and what additional risks should the portfolio manager review?
required_questions: Hedge objective, benchmark and permitted risk budget
Credit and equity losses relative to rate hedge contribution
Basis/curve or nonlinear exposures not captured by parallel first-order DV01
unjustified_conclusions: Positive rates P&L proves effective or optimally sized hedge

cases.question: High-yield spreads widen sharply in the selected stress. Is the resulting portfolio loss a full measure of credit risk, and what evidence is missing?
required_questions: Default/recovery or migration loss beyond linear CS01
Market liquidity and exit costs for HY positions
unjustified_conclusions: CS01 spread P&L measures total default loss

cases.question: During market stress, derivative marks look small relative to notionals. What does that imply for counterparty and funding vulnerability?
required_questions: Netting sets, counterparty exposures and collateral arrangements
Variation/initial margin cash requirements and timing
Gross notional and signed mark do not alone measure payment obligations
unjustified_conclusions: Gross notional is cash due or marks fully determine counterparty risk

cases.question: Suppose yields fall sharply while corporate spreads and equities decline. What alternative explanations and unmodeled exposures should be investigated before deciding why?
required_questions: Growth scare versus liquidity-driven safe-asset demand as hypotheses, not identified causes
Correlated credit/equity downside and diversification assumptions
Evidence for transmission (flows, funding conditions, market depth)
unjustified_conclusions: Observed portfolio P&L uniquely identifies the macroeconomic cause

cases.question: Can the portfolio be considered resilient because its rate-only stress produces a gain? What else needs investigation?
required_questions: Joint rates/credit/equities/FX shocks rather than rate-only gains
Opposite rate-direction stress and exposure asymmetry or convexity
Funding/liquidity requirements under joint adverse conditions
unjustified_conclusions: Rate-only gain proves resilience across crises
